newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian PM backs Fischer, Moore, Fahey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian PM backs Fischer, Moore, Fahey.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday that Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer, Industry Minister John Moore and Finance Minister John Fahey had not breached his rules against ministerial conflict of interest.
"My position is very simply this: that John Moore has not breached the guidelines," Howard told Perth radio 6PR.
"I don't believe Tim Fischer has breached the guidelines," he said. "(Fahey) has just done nothing wrong."
Two members of the government have quit this week for holding shares that could have benefited from their ministerial decisions.
It was aburd to suggest that Fischer was wrong to have held resource shares after he became trade minister in March, Howard said.

"The logic of that is that the minister for trade can't hold any shares at all because any company listed on the Australian Stock Exchange is potentially involved in trade -- they might be selling something overseas or they might be selling something in competition to imports from abroad."
Fischer said earlier that he had complied with the guidelines.
Howard said on Tuesday that the guidelines might have to be changed to allow ministers to use blind trusts, which would prevent them knowing what investments they held.
